steps: Decrease by 1 each time.
After 11 comes 10; after 7 comes 6.

questions.prompt: Circle the larger number in (2,4) and (21,12).
steps: 4 is greater than 2.
21 has 2 tens, while 12 has 1 ten.

questions.prompt: Count the four pictured groups and write the counts in words.
steps: Count each item once.
Upper shoes 7, lower shoes 6; upper balloons 3, lower balloons 9.
questions.answer: Seven shoes; six shoes; three balloons; nine balloons.

questions.prompt: Label the two abacus rods by place value.
steps: The right rod is ones.
The rod to its left is tens, with 4 beads, so the displayed number is 40.

questions.prompt: Write thirteen and eighty-one in numerals.
steps: Thirteen = 10 + 3.
Eighty-one = 80 + 1.

questions.prompt: Circle the sign used for addition from -, =, +.
steps: Addition combines quantities.
Its sign is plus.

questions.prompt: Insert the operation: 51 [ ] 32 = 19.
steps: Test subtraction: 51 - 32 = 19.
Addition would give 83.

questions.prompt: Find balls in all, balls falling and balls not falling.
steps: Count 6 balls in all; 3 are falling.
6 - 3 = 3 remain on the table.

questions.prompt: Find fish by the rock, more fish coming and fish in all.
steps: Count 4 fish by the rock and 4 coming.

questions.prompt: How many legs do two cows have altogether?
steps: Each cow has 4 legs.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number: 45 + [ ] = 71.
Write few or many below the paired pencil and chicken groups.
steps: The pencil groups have 5 and 6, so 5 is fewer.
The chicken groups have 4 and 2, so 4 is more.
questions.answer: Pencils: few, many. Chickens: many, few.

questions.prompt: Write a number sentence for the blocks, then their tens-and-ones regrouping.
steps: There are 8 blocks above and 5 below: 8 + 5 = 13.
Regroup 10 blocks as one ten, leaving 3 ones.

questions.prompt: Who is fifth in the race: Sipho, Lerato, John, Peter, Ann?
steps: The labels show Lerato second and John third.
Continue left to right: Peter fourth, Ann fifth.

questions.prompt: Put crosses on objects that can roll.
steps: Round balls roll because their surfaces are curved.
The boxes and brick have flat faces.
questions.answer: Cross the blue ball, tennis ball and basketball.

questions.prompt: Lebo has 5 crayons and Peter has 8. Who has fewer?
steps: Compare the quantities: 5 < 8.
Lebo has the smaller amount.

questions.prompt: State whether the circle and triangle have round or straight boundaries.
steps: The circle has a curved boundary.
The triangle is bounded by three straight sides.

questions.prompt: Trace the dotted triangle and circle.
steps: Follow all three straight sides of the triangle.
Follow the whole curved boundary of the circle and close it.
questions.answer: A complete traced triangle and a complete traced circle.

questions.prompt: Draw a rectangle.
steps: Draw two parallel horizontal lines.
Join their ends with two parallel vertical lines, making four right angles.
questions.answer: A closed rectangle with opposite sides equal and four right angles.

questions.prompt: How many sides do the circle and square have?
steps: A square has four straight sides.
A circle has no straight sides, but one continuous curved boundary.
questions.answer: Circle: 0 straight sides (1 curved boundary). Square: 4 sides.

questions.prompt: How many angles do the square and circle have?
steps: A square has four corners, each a right angle.
A circle has no corners.

questions.prompt: Count each animal in the picture: cow, zebra, cat, pig and mouse.
steps: Count each animal in the large picture, excluding the small answer-column examples.
There is 1 cow, 2 zebras, 5 cats, 3 pigs and 3 mice.

summaries.Numbers and calculations: Read each value and unit carefully. Align place values and check calculations by reversing the operation. For pictures, count only the requested objects.
